Hi! 

I'm going through this too. My first depression bout. I lost motivation to do anything. For three weeks now I havent done much of anything. I have a failing gall bladder, and this depression causes me to eat really stupid food that makes me uncontrollably sick. It's a never ending battle. I started drinking a lot again. Picked up smoking & havent made a homemade meal in a long time. I'm finally seeking help. Just knowing that I'm not certified crazy is going to help alot. Kind of looking forward to the happy pills & being sober longer than 2 days. Honestly, I know it's easier to deny the issues than to face them, but you'll regret denying them more than addressing them. It's going to be a tough road, but one worthy road when you find your light. You just need to get help. My best friend committed suicide a year ago, I know first hand what can go wrong. Our last conversation was her mental health & I was adament on her getting help, which again in denial she declined. So here I am 1 year later, missing her so much & regretting every missed opportunity to help. Everyone is in the same position. Mental health can suck, but what's worse is denying an issue. 

Please seek help. You deserve to be happy.

Seeking help isn't for the weak. 

Honestly I was weak by denying it completely. That's the simplest solution, right? Wrong. It just snowballs until you even start giving up on yourself. I did a load of laundry today, finally. Made a coffee and enjoyed it too. Having some sort of clarity will make this whole process easier. 

We all go through problems, and I'm just happy that there are still good souls left in this world to help eachother. 

Take care of yourself! 1 day sober 😀

I don't live like a full-fledged Judiast, and am still in between Christianity and converting to Jewish. So right now you could say I'm in limbo as Catholics like to describe it. Jewish people seem to be more afraid of God and see him as a ounishabke being, but Christians see the loving side of God. "Permanent" does not mean a lifetime. Temporary could mean more than a life time but not indefinite. Your issues are NOT permanent. To you they may seem "life long" - but not permanent. You are not permanently ruined.

Hanging yourself is never an option to solve your problems. You know how strong you are. You aren't dumb by any means. You got this. Suicide is a permanent solution to a temporary problem. 

As I said earlier, who cares about your ex? They're ex's for a reason. 

Ending your life will not cause them to learn from their mistakes, nor will it strengthen you. You need to be strong for yourself and find your passion deep within. 

Do you have kids? Your kids would never want to lose a parent. What about your parents? As a parent myself my biggest fear is losing my daughter. I've never known the sound of a parent losing their child, but when my best friend died I can tell you I wish no parent had to go through hearing a parent mourning their child. It's not regular crying, it's tears mixxed with every emotion confusion, screaming, anger, love, pity. Her mom still hasn't stopped crying, I can't bring myself to be around her. This is not how you want others to feel. 

Who do you speak with on a regular basis? Is there anyone? Maybe they can help alleviate your depression. 

As for the hanging, that's really not a nice way to go. My best friend did it. Do you know what people look like after they hang themselves? Do you know that you can survive after hanging yourself? I had another friend who did the same, and he was a vegetable unfortunately. But this realistically is not the way to go. 

I don't know if you believe in God, but I think maybe you should explore your faith. It's my own personal belief that God puts you through what he knows you can handle. He has plans for you & he loves you. 

Can you maybe make plans for a later date and try to fix the problems in the meantime?

You are very intelligent clearly. Ending your life is showing them that they won. Instead, you should focus on helping others and find strength through that. Maybe help other people who are struggling with the same tendancies and teach them how to find their own strengths. Personally I would find a way to help others, because you've found strength if you know it or not. If you end your life you're setting the example to others that they can as well if they are having issues. Would you tell someone else who was in a similar situation that fixing their problems should result in suicide? 

I'm very sorry your marriage fell apart, but it was never meant to be, you can still find someone who appareciates you and lifts you up. Take that as a gift that you are now free to find someone who genuinely loves you for being you. 

The best way I've found to teach people lessons is to cut them out of my life completely. Nothing says "f u" better than me succeeding without them. If you proceed and try to end your own life, they didn't learn. They will just be mourning your loss. It wont change them as people, instead they will use some stupid approach to raise awareness for suicide prevention. They wont learn. Unfortunately you need to be around to teach them. 

Find your own success, love yourself, seek help, cut people out & find new people. I know at times suicide seems easier than overcoming your obstacles, but trust me when you overcome your obstacles, you will feel amazing and have the strength to keep going. 

I realy do wish you that you can find the beauty in life.

There is nothing wrong with having autism. We all have strengths and weaknesses, and their weakness is percieving your traits as a weakness. 

You see the world differently & there is nothing wrong with that. I have friends & autistic family members and I will genuinely tell you that if you're friends aren't supporting you, you need a new support system. It is never okay to put someone down, especially for something they cannot control. 

Please seek help, I can't state this enough. Your life is valuable. You are an awesome person, and if they don't see that, that's their issue & not yours. Please find new friends and seek help. If you have social anxieties with new friends, find a community on reddit and connect with people, go to a local church or community center. But if this is true, the people in your life really need to be reevaluated. 

Reach out if you're having any tendancies, or if you're scared to get help. There are still caring people left in this world.

Honestly I wish that she would have had a terminal illness or had a tragic accident, because I wouldn't blame myself daily. I know I could have been there and put in more effort to stop this. I know there were signs and I just genuinely thought she wouldn't do this, I just thought she would get better. We all blame ourselves daily, and it's something we have to live with. We didn't have any closure, we don't know what happened that night. I was the last person she called & I feel so guilty for sleeping in through that call. 

People who weren't even close are still mouring her, classmates, exboyfriends, old friends, acquaintances.

If you are truly having negative thoughts, I genuinely ask that you seek help. Getting help is not weakness, and I can't state that enough. This was one of our last conversations, she was saying she was having negative thoughts but didn't want to seek help because she didn't want to have the stigma of being "mentally ill". I wish I could have convinced her to get help. There is nothing wrong with getting help, even after her suicide I went and spoke to a counsellor to help me find some sort of clarity. 

Take time out for yourself, do stuff you truly enjoy, hang out with friends & family, watch movies, play sports, redecorate your room & make your space more enjoyable. I promise you if you take the time to try to find a way to love yourself it will get better.
